name: Oregon
overview: Oregon does not sell tax liens or tax certificates to investors. Once property taxes have been delinquent for three years, the county forecloses its tax lien, and the owner and certain other parties then have two years after the foreclosure judgment to redeem by paying the taxes with interest, a five percent penalty and a fee. Property that is not redeemed is deeded to the county, which takes title free of most liens and encumbrances. The county may later sell it: the county board sets a minimum price, the sheriff publishes notice once a week for four consecutive weeks, and the property goes to the highest and best bidder, for cash or with at least 10 percent down on a contract of up to 20 years; land that does not sell may later be sold privately for no less than the largest bid. Sale proceeds are held in a separate interest-bearing account until any surplus owed to the former owner is determined, and an unclaimed surplus goes to the State Treasurer as unclaimed property.

counties.how_to_bid: Auctions are in person. Bidders register at the door on auction day by completing a Bidder Registration Form before the 10:00 AM start (doors open 9:00 AM; no late registrations). Bidding starts at the minimum bid, typically 70 percent of the assessed real market value. The winning bidder pays a nonrefundable 20% deposit at the auction in cash, cashier's check or certified funds, with the balance due at closing, typically 30 to 60 days later; the county conveys by quitclaim deed.

counties.next_sale_note: No sale date posted. Lane County holds auctions as needed with no set time of year; notice is published weekly for four weeks in the Register Guard and posted on the Property Management page one month before a sale.
counties.how_to_bid: Public auctions use sealed bids: one bid per property per bidder, opened and read on the auction date; do not send funds with the bid. The winning bidder's 20% deposit must be received within 24 hours of the bid opening and the balance within 5 business days. Property not sold after two public auctions may be sold privately through the Property Management Officer, with full payment in certified funds. Properties are sold as is.

counties.address: 434 NE Evans Street, McMinnville, OR 97128 (mail: 535 NE Fifth Street, McMinnville, OR 97128)
counties.next_sale_note: No auction date posted. The county says there is no set time of year for auctions and notices go out at least one month before one; residential tax-foreclosed properties are first listed with a licensed broker for twelve months before auction.
counties.how_to_bid: In-person public auctions at the Yamhill County Courthouse. Registration opens at least 30 minutes before the auction: show valid ID, give contact information and accept the county's auction terms to get a bid card. Bring cash or a cashier's check for 20% of the minimum advertised price for each property you want; the winner pays the balance within two business days. Unsold or small non-buildable properties may be sold by private sealed-bid sale with a 10% deposit and the balance due within ten business days of the Board's acceptance.

counties.how_to_bid: Surplus (tax-foreclosed) lands are sold at a public sealed-bid auction to the highest and best bidder at or above the minimum bid, under ORS 275.110 and by order of the Board of Commissioners; Sheriff's auction notices run in the newspaper for four consecutive weeks beforehand. For properties under $20,000, payment is cash or cash equivalents with a 20% deposit of the bid offer; for $20,000 or more, 20% cash down at the sale with the balance on a Land Sale Contract of 3 to 5 years in equal monthly installments (9% per annum administration fee). Registration steps not stated. Sign up for sale notices through the county's Citizen Request Center.
